title: Sugarcane Production, Trench Planting & Ratoon Crop Management
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (IISR), Lucknow
region: Sub-tropical (UP, Bihar, Punjab) & Tropical (Maharashtra, TN, Karnataka)
content: Sugarcane (Saccharum officinarum) requires deep fertile loamy soil with good drainage, pH 6.5 to 7.8. Planting methods: Trench method (spacing 120-150 cm) or Ring-pit method. Use 3-budded setts (37,500 to 40,000 setts/ha) or single bud chip settling method. Sett treatment: Dip setts in Carbendazim 50 WP (1g/l) or Trichoderma culture for 15 minutes to prevent red rot (Colletotrichum falcatum). Ratoon management protocol: After harvesting plant cane close to ground level, perform stubble shaving with sharp spade. Off-barring (plowing between rows to prune old root system) and trash mulching in alternate rows conserve moisture and suppress weeds. Apply 20% extra nitrogen to ratoon crop compared to plant cane. Earthing up at 90 and 120 days prevents lodging and suppresses late tillers (water shoots). Irrigation interval: 8-10 days in peak summer (formative stage) and 15-20 days in winter. Trash mulching saves up to 30% irrigation water.
